en: O Lord with long lotus-petal eyes, intent on the playful movements of Your beautiful young child;
O Govinda, son of Devakī, whose noble face is adorned by a mass of locks—I bow to You! (1)
O Govinda, son of Devakī, whose dark body is adorned with ornaments beginning with golden anklets and tinkling bells, and whose noble face is beautified by a mass of curly locks—I bow to you. 2.
O son of Devakī, saluted by Nanda, whose beautiful face is adorned with a mass of locks of hair and thick lotuses that terrify the bees—I worship you, Govinda, the son of Devakī. 3.
O Govinda, whose stride is non-dual, servant of the Lord, beloved of Śrī Madhva, most venerable one, salutations!
O Govinda, son of Devakī, whose noble face is adorned by locks of hair, I bow to you. 4.
Thus ends the Govinda-stotra composed by the illustrious Kalyāṇīdevī.
